Hi Alex —

Thanks for the call today — great discussion and appreciate the context on your fraud-detection workflow. Quick recap and proposed next steps focused on the integration architecture we walked through: 

What we covered
- High-level flow: customer events -> feature extractor -> embedding store (ANN) -> candidate retrieval -> LLM reranker + tool calling for structured actions
- SDK options: Python + TypeScript SDKs for request routing, streaming, and structured-output enforcement
- Auth: per-service API keys for dev + short-lived mTLS/STS tokens for production (optional)
- Tool/function calling: model returns structured JSON; Redwood supports declarative tool contracts (name, input_schema, output_schema) + runtime tool dispatch
- Embeddings / reranker: ANN first-pass, then lightweight LLM rerank to reduce token costs and improve precision

Action items / asks from your side
1) Can you share a staging endpoint and a service account (read-only) or temporary API key we can use for a POC?
2) A short example of the candidate documents you want reranked (1-2 JSON examples)
3) Any network/firewall requirements for outbound TLS connections from your infra to our hosted endpoints (we support VPC peering / private link if needed)

Planned Redwood deliverables (what we'll send this week)
- Integration guide (attached) with SDK quickstarts for Python/TS
- Example tool-contract JSON (attached) showing best-practice patterns for parallel tools and error handling
- Proposed PO C architecture diagram and cost/latency estimates

If that looks right, can we schedule a 60‑minute technical deep-dive next week (incl. your infra lead) to walk through the SDK snippet and the tool contract? I can do Wed 10/8 10:00–11:00 PT or Thu 10/9 9:00–10:00 PT.

Thanks Marissa — helpful recap. A few clarifying questions from our infra/eng teams before we lock a deep-dive: 

Auth/identity
- Does Redwood support OIDC-backed short-lived tokens (we prefer not to use long-lived API keys in prod)? Is mTLS required for private deployments?

SDK / routing
- For the SDK quickstart: do you have a minimal snippet that shows structured output validation + tool dispatch? We want to see how the SDK enforces the tool contract at call time.
- Can requests be routed to a pinned model in a particular region (EU/US) and automatically fallback to a cheaper variant if capacity is constrained?

Tool calling / parallelism
- Tool definitions: do you recommend synchronous tool calls from the model (model waits for tool result) or async workflows (model emits a tool invocation event and a separate worker executes it)? Our tasks include a DB lookup (fast) and an external API call (variable latency).
- If we run multiple tools in parallel, how do you recommend we handle partial failures (e.g., one tool times out)?

Embeddings / reranker
- For embeddings storage we use a managed vector DB (we’re evaluating FAISS-based and cloud ANN). Any recommendations for vector dimensionality / index type for short (<= 512 token) docs?
- What does the reranker call look like in practice (do you send full context or only candidates + metadata)?

If you can send the minimal SDK snippet + a sample tool-contract, I’ll share a staging API cred and a couple of candidate docs. Also prefer the deep-dive Wed 10/8 10:00 PT.

From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@finapps.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Cc: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai
Date: Sat, 4 Oct 2025 11:35:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + next steps (SDK/auth/rerank)

Hi Alex — quick technical answers and a minimal snippet to help your engs evaluate. Happy to expand on any point in the deep-dive.

Auth / Tokens
- We support multiple patterns: 1) long-lived API keys (dev), 2) OIDC short-lived tokens via our token exchange (recommended), and 3) mTLS for private/on-prem deployments. For cloud-hosted production we typically recommend OIDC + short-lived tokens to integrate with customer IdPs.

Routing / Model pinning
- SDK supports a "model" parameter per request (e.g., "redwood-llm/fast-reranker-v2"). You can also set routing policies at the API key / project level (region preference, cost tier). Automatic fallback is supported: policy = [preferred model, fallback-quantized-variant].

Structured output + tool contracts (example)
- Tool contract (high level): {"tool_name": "lookup_account", "input_schema": "{account_id: string}", "output_schema": "{balance: number, status: string}"} — Redwood enforces the output_schema at runtime and can validate before calling your tool.
- SDK enforces: validate(output, output_schema) || raise ValidationError -> returns structured error to caller. You can configure: fail-fast vs. sanitize-and-continue.

Minimal Python SDK snippet (conceptual):

from redwood import RedwoodClient, ToolContract

client = RedwoodClient(api_key="<SHORT_LIVED_TOKEN>", region="us-west-2")

# declare tool
lookup = ToolContract(name="lookup_account", input_schema={"account_id": "string"}, output_schema={"balance": "number", "status": "string"})

# call model with tool contracts, structured output enforced
resp = client.chat.create(
    model="redwood-llm/structured-call-v1",
    messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Get account status for 12345"}],
    tools=[lookup],
    max_tokens=300,
    structured_output=True,
    timeout=10.0,  # per-call timeout in seconds
)

if resp.tool_invocations:
    # runtime will return invoked tool name + serialized input for your worker to execute
    for inv in resp.tool_invocations:
        # inv = {"tool_name": "lookup_account", "input": {...}}
        try:
            result = my_worker.execute(inv["tool_name"], inv["input"])
            client.tool.report_result(inv["id"], result)  # ack back to model runtime
        except Exception as e:
            client.tool.report_error(inv["id"], str(e))

Notes on sync vs async / parallel tools
- Synchronous model-led tool calls: model waits for tool result. Simpler for tight request-response but increases latency. Good for fast DB lookups.
- Async event-driven: model emits tool invocation(s); workers process asynchronously and notify the runtime. Good for long-running or side-effecting tasks.
- Parallel execution: we recommend running independent tools in parallel and returning partial results. Use idempotency keys and a per-tool timeout. Redwood supports an invocation-level timeout and retry policy.
- Partial failures: pattern = (1) define critical vs. non-critical tools in the contract, (2) set per-tool timeout + fallback value, (3) on failure return structured error (e.g., {"tool_name":"x","status":"failed","error":"timeout"}) so the model can act deterministically.

Embeddings / reranker pattern
- Store dense vectors in your chosen ANN (HNSW / IVF + PQ recommended depending on scale). For short docs (<=512 tokens) 768–1536 dims typical; tradeoff between precision and index size.
- Retrieval + rerank flow: (1) ANN nearest-neighbors -> (2) fetch candidate docs metadata (ids, small snippet) -> (3) call reranker model with candidates-only + query (not full doc body unless needed) to save tokens.
- Reranker prompt shape: include candidate snippets + metadata, request a score + structured reasons, optionally request a top-1 JSON action that can trigger a tool call.

Attachments: I attached a sample tool-contract JSON and a short patterns doc for embeddings + reranker.

If you can share staging creds and a couple of candidate docs we’ll prepare a runnable example for the deep-dive.

—Dev
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachments: tool-contracts-example.json, embeddings-reranker-patterns.pdf
